rationale:
WHAT THE DEFECT IS. The acceptance runner has a check type, `computed_values`, that fills a tool's inputs and asserts the EXACT TEXT of each output. It is fully wired: whitelisted at internal/adapters/browserrunner/run_checks_action.go:568 and dispatched at :708. The agent that authors every tool's acceptance fence has never been told it exists. `tool-generator`'s compose_plan prompt states a CLOSED vocabulary -- four liveness checks plus one optional `interaction` -- and ends the paragraph "No other check type exists for interactions". So no generated fence can ever compare a number, and a calculator that prints a confidently wrong figure passes Tier 4 with a record that reads PASSED.

MEASURED 2026-09-03 16:04Z on live doc_plans (subject_type='tool', is_current): tool-generator has authored 187 fences; `uses_computed_values` = ZERO; 91 drive inputs; 55 DRIVE INPUTS AND ASSERT NOTHING. All 30 value-asserting fences in the estate were hand-written by an operator or a lane. max(created_at) is the same day, so this is a live intake, not a backlog.

WHY THE INSTRUCTION IS CONDITIONAL AND ITS DEFAULT IS REFUSAL -- this is the part I most want reviewed. `computed_values` is a REGRESSION check by design. Its own contract (run_checks_action.go:790-808) says values "are CAPTURED from the tool while it is known good ... and then defended", and that "a golden captured from an already-wrong tool pins the wrong answer -- the capture script therefore refuses to emit for a tool whose outputs do not react to its inputs". At BIRTH nothing is known good, and this step's only inputs are the spec and {{.generated_html}} -- the very artefact whose correctness is in question. So an unqualified "emit computed_values" instruction could only ever pin whatever the new code prints. That failure has a price on record: bugs_open/224 / bugs_closed/225, an expired GBP625k FTB SDLT cap certified green for sixteen months.

The one oracle actually present at birth is the model's own knowledge of a PUBLISHED formula applied to inputs it chooses. So the prompt licenses exactly that case (standard financial formula, statutory or tax rate, unit conversion, published index, or arithmetic that follows from the spec), requires the working to be shown in ## Dependencies, and requires REFUSAL otherwise with a "No value assertion:" line naming what is missing. Anything that scores, rates, ranks or grades by a heuristic invented for the tool has no independent source and must get no check. The post-verify block enforces the refusal arm's presence: if the guidance is ever edited out, the migration aborts rather than shipping the capability without its brake.

WHY THE CHARACTER CAP MOVES 3000 -> 3600. A computed_values check in the taught shape costs ~350-450 characters of the output document, plus the Dependencies line and two top-level keys. Left at 3000 the model must trade the new assertion against prose it was also told to write -- which is how a fix like this ships as a truncated PLAN. compose_plan runs claude-sonnet-5 at max_tokens 4000; 3600 characters is ~900-1200 tokens, so there is no truncation risk. Note the cap is in CHARACTERS: the live prompt is 2766 characters but 2782 bytes (8 em-dashes), so anyone checking compliance in bytes reads high.

WHY tool-generator ONLY. `experience-planner` also authors fences, but carries them in THREE steps (compose, recompose, reframe) and has authored 3 fences EVER against tool-generator's 187 (measured same run). Three more verbatim anchors for ~1% of the population is a bad trade inside one migration, so it is a deliberate follow-on, recorded as such. Component-subject fences (55, zero value assertions) are recorded as a NEW candidate in bugs_open/449 section 9f and are deliberately not touched here.

TWO BLOCKERS I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, both of which dissolved. (1) bugs_open/441 makes fences go stale against re-rendered ids, and runComputedValues FAILS rather than skips on a missing element (page.Count(sel)==0 -> problems). That risk is real but lives in BACKFILL only: a fence written AT BIRTH has no staleness window, because the generator emits selectors from the template it just wrote and ScopeToolBirthTemplate guarantees the tool carries that template verbatim as rendered_html. This migration touches new fences only; backfill stays deferred. (2) I feared a value assertion would arm Tier 2 to dispatch tool-improver at a shared component. It cannot: evaluateStaticCriteria (platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/check_tool_acceptance.go) has no computed_values arm, so it falls to `default: skip(ch.ID, ch.Type+" is not statically checkable (Tier 4)")`. The shared-component exposure comes from three built-in shell checks that run independent of the criteria, so this change widens it by zero rows. I still teach no_auto_fix, on its own merits: the only way an automated rewriter turns a red arithmetic fence green is by changing numbers on a page quoting tax and consumer credit.

TESTED, NOT ASSERTED. The pair was run against the LIVE row inside a transaction that was rolled back: 2766 chars -> apply -> 5046 -> apply AGAIN (UPDATE 0, "already applied" notice, post-verify still passes) -> reverse -> 2766, byte-identical to baseline. The first cut of the rollback used a regexp and FAILED -- `.` stops at a newline under flag `n` and the pattern had dropped an apostrophe -- and it reported UPDATE 1 while substituting nothing. Only the post-verify DO block caught it. The rollback now swaps the two dollar-quoted literals, extracted programmatically from the migration so they are byte-identical by construction.

PATHS THIS RATIONALE MENTIONS THAT ARE NOT IN THE EDIT LIST, accounted for as the runbook requires: (a) docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/749_..._ROLLBACK.sql -- written and round-trip tested, but `_ROLLBACK` is explicitly out of council scope (it is not the change), so it is not listed as an edit; (b) run_checks_action.go, check_tool_acceptance.go, write_doc_plan_action.go -- READ as evidence, not modified by this change; (c) the lane's five working docs and bugs_open/449 -- prose, out of scope. No Go file is touched by this submission.

plan.risks:
WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK, in the order I think it matters.

1. IS THE REFUSAL ARM STRONG ENOUGH, AND IS IT THE RIGHT SHAPE? This is the whole safety of the change. The prompt says to emit a value assertion ONLY when the expectation can be derived without reading a number off the HTML it was shown, and to omit it otherwise with a "No value assertion:" line. My worry is that an LLM handed a working calculator will find it very easy to believe it has "derived" a figure it in fact read. I have tried to make that harder by requiring the RULE and the WORKING in ## Dependencies, so a reviewer can see the claimed derivation rather than just its output -- but I cannot enforce it in SQL, and I would like a judgement on whether a prompt-level requirement is sufficient here or whether this needs a checker that compares the asserted value against the tool's own rendered output and objects when they match suspiciously. Note the estate's own precedent cuts my way: toolgolden.py's --emit-criteria REFUSES a non-reactive tool, and mcalc's verify_criteria.py reports "NOT VERIFIED (no independent model)" and leaves tool-portfolio with no fence.

2. IS "A PUBLISHED FORMULA THE MODEL KNOWS" AN ACCEPTABLE ORACLE AT BIRTH? It is the only independent source available at this step, and it is genuinely independent of the code. But it is the model's own knowledge, so it is fallible in a way a published register is not, and a wrong "known" rate (a superseded VAT band, an out-of-date threshold) would pin a wrong expectation with full confidence -- which is exactly bugs_open/224's failure mode arriving by a different route. The mitigation I chose is that the rule must be NAMED in Dependencies, so a wrong one is visible to a human rather than buried in a number. I would accept an objection that statutory rates specifically should be excluded from the licensed list, leaving only formulae and conversions.

3. THE CAP CHANGE IS A SECOND, SEPARATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IN ONE MIGRATION. 3000 -> 3600 characters affects EVERY generated PLAN, including the majority that will correctly refuse to write a value assertion and therefore do not need the extra room. I judged that shipping the vocabulary without the budget is the worse failure (it trades the assertion for a truncated document, and truncation is silent), and the pre-guard refuses to apply either half alone. But a reviewer may reasonably hold that a document-length change should be its own migration with its own evidence.

4. BLAST RADIUS IS EVERY TOOL BUILT FROM NOW ON, and it is config, so it is live on apply with no image to roll back. There is no default-OFF switch: the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 says we will not require one, and a prompt instruction has no natural off position. The containment is that the change is ADDITIVE to a prompt whose existing instructions are untouched, and that the refusal branch is the default -- so the expected outcome for most tools is a PLAN identical to today's plus one Dependencies line.

5. WHAT I DID NOT DO, deliberately: no backfill of the 55 standing driving-and-blind fences (that is where bugs_open/441's stale-selector risk actually bites, and runComputedValues fails rather than skips); no change to experience-planner (3 fences ever, 3 anchors); no widening to component-subject fences (55, zero assertions -- filed as a new candidate instead). If a reviewer thinks any of those belong in THIS change rather than after it, that is worth saying now.
